Scope:
- With no `--fencing-token`, a claimant-owned mutation whose target equals NEEDLE_BEAD_ID uses NEEDLE_BEAD_FENCING_TOKEN.
- An explicit flag overrides the environment. The variables never apply to any other issue.
- The audit and change-feed event records the credential source (flag or env).
- label add/remove and dep add/remove accept `--fencing-token`: omission behaves as today, and a supplied token is validated like on fenced surfaces.
- The credential-required error names both remedies.

Acceptance:
- With NEEDLE_BEAD_ID=X and NEEDLE_BEAD_FENCING_TOKEN set to the current credential, update, close, release, reopen and resolve on X succeed without the flag. A stale value in the environment conflicts with exit 4 and changes nothing, exactly like a stale flag.
- With the same environment, a mutation on Y != X behaves exactly as with the variables unset.
- An explicit `--fencing-token` overrides the environment in both directions (stale flag + good env conflicts; good flag + stale env succeeds).
- Accepts the exact value form NEEDLE sends (`fencing_credential.expose()` when present, otherwise the epoch).
- label add/remove and dep add/remove: correct token passes, stale token exits 4 with no change, omission unchanged.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.
issue.title: Read the claim credential from NEEDLE_BEAD_FENCING_TOKEN and accept --fencing-token on every mutation
